summary: Pennsylvania's sitting governor, Josh Shapiro (Democrat), ran again and won a second term, defeating Stacy Garrity (Republican). The AP called the race on election night.

candidates.name: Josh Shapiro
candidates.bio: Josh Shapiro is the governor of Pennsylvania, in office since January 2023. He previously served as state attorney general from 2017 to 2023 and as a Montgomery County commissioner.

positions.summary: Lists raising the minimum wage as one of his second-term priorities and has proposed a 52% tax on skill game machines.
Says federal Medicaid funding cuts would hasten the closing of rural hospitals, which he described as "teetering on the brink of closure."
Says he has increased public education funding and his 2026-27 budget proposes $565 million in adequacy funding for schools.
Says data center developers must pay the full cost of the power they need, meet strict environmental standards, and get local approval before the state reviews their permits.
Says reproductive health care decisions should be made "between patients and doctors, not politicians."

candidates.name: Stacy Garrity
candidates.bio: Stacy Garrity is the Pennsylvania state treasurer, in office since 2021, and a retired U.S. Army Reserve colonel. She was the Republican nominee for governor in 2026.

positions.summary: Says she would cut utility bills by 15% to 25% and cut the property tax burden by one-third within two years.
Says she would lift the ban on new drilling sites on day one and reform or pause renewable energy and efficiency mandates.
Says she would pass Lifeline Scholarships, opt in to the federal scholarship tax credit program, and put parents in control of their children's education.
Has embraced the 2025 federal law, with her campaign saying its Medicaid changes strengthen Medicaid by "cracking down on fraud, waste, abuse, and improper enrollment."

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called). Shares refreshed Nov. 25 from thegreenpapers.com, unofficial.
